skill.name: prune-tests
skill.description: Prune tests that guard no behavior.
skill.summary: Remove redundant tests and rewrite implementation-focused assertions around intended behavior.
skill.author: caldoai

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, not shell execution. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration. The skill directs test and production-code deletion, so users should review proposed removals against behavioral requirements.

static_findings.snippet: - It tests the browser: a `<button>` renders, or a click event fires. The browser is already tested.

content.user_title: Prune Tests That Do Not Protect Behavior
content.value_statement: Redundant and implementation-focused tests increase maintenance without reliably protecting intended behavior. This skill guides test removal and rewrites around observable outcomes.
actual_capabilities: Evaluate whether tests depend on intended behavior, removed code, ineffective assertions, or implementation details.
Identify duplicate tests that guard the same behavior.
Rewrite assertions about private state or internal calls around observable behavior.
Replace expected values derived from production logic with explicit expected outcomes.
Direct removal of production helpers that exist only for deleted tests.
limitations: Provides written instructions and examples, not a bundled test runner or coverage analyzer.
Requires repository context and intended requirements to judge whether tests protect meaningful behavior.
Does not guarantee that pruning preserves coverage or detects every regression.
Production-code removals require independent review of callers and operational uses.

use_cases.title: Reduce maintenance after feature removal
use_cases.description: Review tests for removed features and distinguish obsolete assertions from remaining behavioral requirements.

use_cases.title: Improve assertion quality
use_cases.description: Find assertions that repeat implementation logic or inspect private state, then propose behavior-focused replacements.

use_cases.title: Review duplicate coverage
use_cases.description: Compare overlapping tests and identify removals while checking whether distinct contracts or edge cases remain protected.

prompt_templates.title: Review one test file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [test file] using prune-tests. List each test, its intended behavior, and whether to keep, rewrite, or remove it without editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand candidate changes before applying them.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite implementation-focused assertions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [test file] for private-state assertions and expected values copied from implementation logic. Rewrite them around documented behavior while preserving meaningful cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve existing tests without broad deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Compare overlapping tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare tests under [path] for duplicate behavioral coverage. Explain equivalent inputs, outcomes, and contracts before proposing removals; keep distinct edge cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate redundancy across multiple test files.

prompt_templates.title: Prune a scoped suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply prune-tests within [path] against [requirements]. Rewrite meaningful assertions, justify deletions, verify production-helper callers, and report test results or unavailable validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: perform a scoped cleanup with explicit verification.

output_examples.input: Review a discount test whose expected result repeats the discount calculation.
output: Decision: Rewrite the assertion rather than delete the test.
Behavior: A price of 100 with a 20 percent discount should produce 80.
Reason: An explicit expected result avoids reproducing the same calculation mistake.

output_examples.input: Review a cart test that checks the private item array after adding a book.
output: Decision: Replace the private-state assertion with an observable outcome.
Proposed assertion: For an initially empty cart, adding one book makes the total equal its price.
Review note: Confirm that this outcome matches the documented cart behavior.

best_practices: Document the intended behavior and remaining coverage before deleting a test.
Check callers before removing production helpers, and keep changes within the requested scope.
Run relevant tests after edits and review the diff for lost behavioral or security coverage.
anti_patterns: Deleting tests solely because their names, setup, or assertions look similar.
Assuming negative tests or removed-feature checks cannot protect current requirements.
Removing production helpers without checking callers outside the tests being pruned.

faq.question: What does prune-tests do?
faq.answer: It guides an assistant to remove tests without behavioral value and rewrite meaningful tests that depend on implementation details.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include a test runner?
faq.answer: No. It contains instructions and a diff example, not executable tooling for running tests or measuring coverage.

faq.question: Can I limit the review to one directory?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill accepts an optional path, so you can request a focused review.

faq.question: Can it delete production code?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs removal of production code that exists only for removed tests. Verify callers and requirements before accepting those changes.

faq.question: Should I remove every negative or duplicate-looking test?
faq.answer: No. Confirm that each candidate lacks a distinct required behavior, including security and regression protections, before deleting it.
